question: What drove bank overdrafts from R364m (audited 30 Sep 2025) to R2,273m (unaudited 31 Mar 2026), and is any portion a reclassification from interest-bearing debt? What are the facility limits, maturities and drawn/undrawn split at 31 Mar 2026?
evidence_required: Overdraft and short-term facility balances, limits, maturities, drawn/undrawn split, and any reclassification disclosure, Rm, at 31 Mar 2026 vs 30 Sep 2025 and 31 Mar 2025
closure_condition: Driver of the R1.9bn overdraft increase and facility detail disclosed, or confirmed not disclosed; benign explanations (seasonal PBD funding, reclass) acceptable. Forecast consequence: liquidity and refinancing risk, net debt trajectory.
answer: Note 2 shows bank overdrafts of R273m at 31 Mar 2026, not R2,273m; overdrafts fell R91m from R364m at 30 Sep 2025 (273-364=-91). No R1.9bn increase exists in this note. Total undrawn overdraft facilities rose to R475m (Sep-25 R136m; Mar-25 R43m). Overdraft facility limits/maturities and drawn/undrawn split for term debt are not itemised here.

question: What is the measurement basis of purchased book debts (amortised cost, FVTPL or POCI) and how does the R4,489m carrying value at 31 Mar 2026 reconcile to the PBD roll-forward (opening, acquisitions, collections, amortisation, closing)?
evidence_required: PBD measurement basis, roll-forward in Rm for H1 2026 and H1 2025, and reconciliation to the R4,489m / R4,353m / R4,677m carrying values
closure_condition: Basis and roll-forward disclosed and reconciling to the statement of financial position, or confirmed not disclosed; forecast consequence: amortisation projection and credit-loss treatment.
answer: p.27 shows principal book portfolio at amortised cost with carrying value equal to disclosed fair value (Level 3): R3,845m (31 Mar 2026), R3,690m (31 Mar 2025), R3,975m (30 Sep 2025). p.28 confirms a separate pool of purchased book debts is measured at FVTPL (R644m, Level 3) because collections are not solely P&I. The amortised-cost principal-book roll-forward (opening/acquisitions/collections/amortisation/closing) is not in this capture.

evidence.quote: Certain purchased book debts (other financial assets) are managed on a fair value basis.

question: Do the group's purchased book debts fall within POCI, amortised cost or FVTPL, and does the generic contractual-cash-flow ECL policy in Note 6.1 (discounted at original EIR, max contractual period) actually apply to PBD, or is a lifetime-ECL-since-initial-recognition / fair-value model used instead? Provide the PBD measurement basis and any POCI credit-risk classification disclosure.
target_section: D003.4 Note 1 Purchased book debts (p.13); D003.1 statement of financial position (p.8)
evidence_required: Explicit measurement basis for PBD (POCI/amortised cost/FVTPL), whether lifetime ECL since initial recognition applies, and any POCI credit-risk classification; Rm carrying values at 31 Mar 2026 vs 30 Sep 2025 vs 31 Mar 2025
closure_condition: PBD measurement basis and applicable ECL model stated and reconciled to the carrying value, or confirmed not disclosed; benign explanations (PBD held at FVTPL with separate ECL on other assets) acceptable. Forecast consequence: credit-loss treatment, amortisation projection and earnings volatility.
answer: PBDs are classified as purchased credit-impaired (POCI), Stage 3, at initial recognition; classification irrevocable. Measured at amortised cost using a credit-adjusted EIR (weighted average 19.2% at 31 Mar 2026; 17.9% at 31 Mar 2025; 18.4% at 30 Sep 2025). Changes in lifetime ECLs recognised in P&L; favourable changes recognised as impairment gain even below initial-recognition ECL. Other financial assets within PBD are at fair value. Principal book net carrying value: R3,845m (31 Mar 2026), R3,690m (31 Mar 2025), R3,975m (30 Sep 2025).

evidence.quote: PBDs are classified as purchased credit-impaired (POCI) financial assets (stage 3) on initial recognition
The weighted average credit-adjusted effective interest rate at period end is 19.2% (31 March 2025: 17.9%; 30 September 2025: 18.4%).

answer: FVTPL purchased-book-debt pool roll-forward now available (opening 702, gains 30, other movements -88, closing 644 for Mar-26; additions 28, collections 116). This is the FVTPL pool, not the amortised-cost principal book; principal-book roll-forward and ECL-release driver split still not disclosed in this capture.
